purpose: S4 for batch 3: the first-public minute of each release in the third batch, taken from the public wire page, and what was found on the way. config/m5-phase1b-events.json now holds the ten events built from it in the dry-run state after the nineteen of batches 1 and 2: sealed, no attestations, so each quarantines on FIRST_PUBLIC_TIME_UNVERIFIED until the owner attests it. Nothing here is a price, a return or a label.

permission.read_as: Batch 3 only: the public pages of the releases of the ten candidates listed below on Business Wire, GlobeNewswire, PR Newswire or Accesswire, or on the issuer's own newsroom, to take each release's first-public minute, and a check for a separate same-day release. In the built-in browser, in browser memory only; the URL, the displayed minute and a short excerpt are kept. No web-search tool, no price or quote page, no filing. It carries no push and no other download; later batches ask again.

reading.what: The ten releases' pages and company searches on GlobeNewswire, Business Wire and PR Newswire (each issuer's wire is the one its earlier events in the repository used); held in browser memory only; the URL, the displayed minute, the page's machine-readable time and the same-day check results are kept. No filing was opened: EDGAR's acceptance times come from the archived SEC lists already in the repository. Listings were read through short extractions of the dates, times and titles wanted, so as to see as little else as possible.
reading.what_was_seen_in_passing: Business Wire's 'Okta Announces' listing was read as page text before I narrowed the extractions: it showed the headline, the time (2026-08-26 16:01 ET) and the first sentences of Okta's 2026-08-26 release, which is a candidate of a later batch, and the blurbs of older Okta releases. I did not open that release's page and did not use what I saw; the later batch will read its own page if the owner permits it. Other extractions returned titles of neighbouring releases (for Alkami, Neurocrine, Huron, CACI, Viasat) and one dateline sentence of Lovesac's release that gives its quarter's net sales. These are company-reported business content, not a price, a return or a label of any event.
reading.refused_or_missing: Nothing was refused. Two Business Wire searches returned nothing, one wasted page load each: the first Okta search used a wrong title ('Okta Announces Fiscal First Quarter 2027 Financial Results'; the real one is 'Okta Announces First Quarter Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Results'), and 'Viasat Reports' found nothing because Viasat's releases are on GlobeNewswire ('Viasat Releases ...'). On one CACI listing the date lines did not render (a dash), so the neighbours' dates there come from their addresses.

next: A sealed dry run (the push of the events file starts it; the nineteen pinned events of batches 1 and 2 are re-checked in the same run), then the signoff packet for the owner: for each event the wire evidence above and the sealed run's facts (missing and zero-volume sessions, corporate actions), and any call for the owner's word; then the owner's attestations of first-public time, historical identity and corporate actions, and the attested sealed run that pins each event's commitment.
what_this_is_not: Not an attestation: first-public time, historical identity and corporate actions are the owner's to attest, per batch.
Not a proof that nothing earlier was public: open-web research can show no discoverable earlier disclosure, not a negative.
Not a price, a return or a label of any event: none was read; the sealed run prints none.
